metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast upward; correct by reducing forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 days.
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.5) after a downtrend, model often under-responds; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 2–4 days.
- Model consistently under-forecasts in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or event-driven; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.4 or event imminent.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price correction), model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >15% above 14-day moving average, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize support; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
